title: Hurricane Ike Search and Rescue Operations
description: B-roll of a helicopter ride off of the Gulf Coast area after Hurricane Ike. Scenes include Soldiers looking from the helicopter down at the flooded area and a short interview. Produced by Spc. Katherine Danielson.

transcript.text: Seagrapes, S-E-O-G-R-A-V-E-N-M-E-A-A-T-60 instructor pilot for the Charlie 108th assault company and I'm also the Austin aviation support facility standardization officer.
We a little bit about what y'all are doing here for Hurricane Ike.
Currently we're part of the Texas Task Force 1 search and rescue recovery effort.
We spent the last several days in and around the state recovery picked up off of all of our island accounts.
And have y'all picked anybody up so far?
Yes, we picked a total of, two days ago we picked a total of eight up of our aircraft.
And do you know how many people have been rescued total?
I do not. I have not heard any for some weeks.
Okay. What goes into an operation like this like rescuing people?
You have, well, prior to any event you have all the train up this require between us and as a flight crew as well as interagency training with Texas Task Force 1.
You also have the logistics and planning, pre-existing resources, maintenance and fuel and things like that.
Okay. And when you go in to a storm or a right after a storm for the recovery, what is going on when it's all entailed and picking people up and bringing them on board?
And how do you keep them calm? What kind of goes into that?
The crew members in the back are departmental and responsible for that.
Obviously the crew members have pilots up front, just flying the aircraft.

pass_reason: Ike helicopter ride and interview; Ike already ran twice this week
